definition.normative_voice: An OntologySubject is one identity-bearing node or relation whose semantic history is recorded in exactly one canonical subject event stream.
definition.formal_voice: OntologySubject = OntologyNode | OntologyRelation; canonical_stream_count(subject) = 1.
definition.operational_interpretation: Use the subject identity to select the event chain that calculates one node or relation state.
definition.plain_language_voice: The specific node or relation whose history we are following.
definition.domain_context_voice: In CyberAlchemy Lab, the reducer calculates each subject independently before it assembles an ontology cut.
definition.boundary: A subject is not its mutable document, latest snapshot, projection row, label, or directory path.

definition.normative_voice: An OntologyNode is an OntologySubject that carries one stable node identity and a complete resulting semantic state specialized by one closed ontology-type profile.
definition.formal_voice: OntologyNode = (OntologySubjectIdentity, OntologySemanticState, profile_ref), where profile_ref resolves to one closed profile.
definition.operational_interpretation: Append a complete semantic state event when the node meaning changes; calculate the current node by replaying its stream.
definition.plain_language_voice: A typed meaning-bearing item whose current state comes from its own event history.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy ontology nodes may represent business meaning, runtime meaning, premises, authority, evidence, projections, or residue through closed profiles.
definition.boundary: A node is not its governance posture and must not infer authority from status, location, shared context, or label equality.

definition.normative_voice: An OntologyRelation is a first-class OntologySubject whose complete semantic state names one typed directed or symmetric link and its exact source and target node identities.
definition.formal_voice: OntologyRelation = (identity, relation_type_ref, lifecycle, source_node_id, target_node_id, direction, typed_properties, forbidden_collapse).
definition.operational_interpretation: Give each relation its own semantic event stream and validate both endpoints in the same ontology cut.
definition.plain_language_voice: A relationship with its own identity and history, not a loose link hidden inside a node.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy Lab replays relation subjects beside node subjects and rejects active relations whose endpoints are absent from the selected cut.
definition.boundary: Do not infer a relation from labels, directories, co-occurrence, shared context, or an embedded challenge graph.

definition.normative_voice: OntologySubjectIdentity is the stable tuple that identifies one node or relation independently of its label, lifecycle, current state, location, and projections.
definition.formal_voice: OntologySubjectIdentity = (subject_id, ontology_id, subject_kind, type_ref), with subject_id unique within ontology_id.
definition.operational_interpretation: Use the tuple to derive the subject stream and to reject cross-ontology or cross-kind identity collisions.
definition.plain_language_voice: The permanent address of one node or relation.
definition.domain_context_voice: For a node, subject_id is node_id and type_ref is node_type_ref; for a relation, they are relation_id and relation_type_ref.
definition.boundary: Identity does not change when a label, definition, status, owner, or projection changes.

definition.normative_voice: OntologySemanticState is the complete meaning-bearing state that one accepted semantic event says an OntologySubject has after that event.
definition.formal_voice: state(subject, event_n) = event_n.complete_resulting_semantic_state; prior state is not patched at read time.
definition.operational_interpretation: Validate the whole resulting state, append it, and select the latest valid event at or before the requested cursor.
definition.plain_language_voice: Everything the node or relation means after one event.
definition.domain_context_voice: For nodes this includes lifecycle, label, definition or claim, scope, semantic components, definition references, typed properties, use obligations, and forbidden collapses.
definition.boundary: Semantic state excludes provenance, confidence, promotion, authority, challenge handling, conflicts, and governance residue.

definition.normative_voice: OntologyGovernanceState is the calculated governance facet for one exact semantic event epoch, derived only from valid governance events that reference that epoch exactly.
definition.formal_voice: governance_state(e) = fold(valid governance events g where g.semantic_ref = (id(e), digest(e), cursor(e))).
definition.operational_interpretation: Validate each exact reference before applying provenance, owner, status, authority, confidence, challenge, conflict, drift, invalidation, or residue changes.
definition.plain_language_voice: The current governed posture attached to one exact version of meaning.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy Lab calculates this facet separately so governance work cannot rewrite semantic history.
definition.boundary: Governance state is not semantic state, does not grant authority by itself, and cannot join by subject ID alone.

definition.normative_voice: GovernedOntologyNodeView is a deterministic read model that combines one node identity, its latest valid semantic state through a selected cursor, the valid governance state for that exact semantic epoch, and source projection metadata.
definition.formal_voice: view(node,c) = identity(node) + latest_semantic(node,c) + governance(exact_ref(latest_semantic)) + projection_metadata.
definition.operational_interpretation: Build the view from canonical event streams and fail closed when a selected semantic or governance dependency is missing, stale, ambiguous, or mismatched.
definition.plain_language_voice: The complete calculated node that a governed consumer can read.
definition.domain_context_voice: This is the object exposed to CyberAlchemy contexts; it carries source cursor and digest data so consumers can trace it back to events.
definition.boundary: The view is not a replay source, independent truth, promotion verdict, or alternate context-owned node.

definition.normative_voice: This pack reuses CAV2-D40 without amendment: a challenge contract declares how an object can be challenged, contradicted, validated, blocked, or routed for owner review without silently changing meaning or confidence.
definition.formal_voice: ChallengeContract = (challenge_response, valid_challenge_modes, contradiction_edges, validation_edges, owner_route, resolution_gate, blocking_questions, challenge_residue_route).
definition.operational_interpretation: Require the complete contract when a candidate node may become load-bearing, and route every unresolved challenge through its named gate or residue route.
definition.plain_language_voice: The node's instructions for how to disagree with it correctly.
definition.domain_context_voice: The governed-node model stores the challenge contract beside confidence and residue, never inside either one.
definition.boundary: It is not confidence, proof, a verdict, promotion, authority, or the object's own residue.

definition.normative_voice: A RelationEndpoint is an exact OntologyNode identity occupying the source or target role of one OntologyRelation.
definition.formal_voice: RelationEndpoint = (role in {source,target}, node_id, ontology_id); endpoint.ontology_id = relation.ontology_id.
definition.operational_interpretation: Resolve both endpoint identities in the same selected ontology cut before admitting an active relation into that cut.
definition.plain_language_voice: One of the two exact nodes that a relation connects.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy Lab uses endpoint identities instead of embedded node copies or label-based joins.
definition.boundary: An endpoint is not a label, selector result, directory path, or implied node.

definition.normative_voice: RelationEndpointIntegrity is the invariant that every active relation has valid source and target node identities present and active in the same consistent ontology cut.
definition.formal_voice: active(r,cut) implies exists active source(r) in cut and exists active target(r) in cut.
definition.operational_interpretation: Reject or classify as typed residue any relation whose endpoint cannot be resolved at the selected cursor.
definition.plain_language_voice: A live relation cannot point to a missing node.
definition.domain_context_voice: The ontology-at-cursor projection checks endpoint integrity after calculating node and relation states at one cut.
definition.boundary: Endpoint presence at another cursor or in another context does not satisfy this invariant.

definition.normative_voice: A ContextSelector is a source-bound request for one bounded ontology view that names an exact semantic cursor, required subject set, governance join policy, intended use, and projection profile.
definition.formal_voice: ContextSelector = (semantic_cursor, required_subject_set, governance_join_policy, intended_use, projection_profile).
definition.operational_interpretation: Resolve every required subject and valid governance join at the named cursor, then apply only the selected projection profile.
definition.plain_language_voice: A precise request for which part of the ontology a context needs and at what point.
definition.domain_context_voice: A CyberAlchemy Context uses the selector to calculate a view without creating its own ontology truth.
definition.boundary: A selector does not add canonical fields, fork identity, change lifecycle, or grant authority.

definition.normative_voice: A ContextProjection is a deterministic bounded read model produced by one ContextSelector and carrying the source cursor, event-set digest, selected subject identities, and forbidden authority moves.
definition.formal_voice: ContextProjection = project(ontology_at(selector.cursor), selector.subjects, selector.profile, selector.join_policy).
definition.operational_interpretation: Filter or render the consistent source view while retaining the metadata needed to reproduce and audit the result.
definition.plain_language_voice: The exact slice of the ontology calculated for one context.
definition.domain_context_voice: Two CyberAlchemy contexts may calculate different projections from the same event history without forking that history.
definition.boundary: A context projection is not canonical state, a replay source, a lifecycle verdict, or an authority decision.

records.decision_owner_route: CyberAlchemy Lab semantic and governance stream owners

definition.normative_voice: An ExactSemanticEventReference is the indivisible tuple of semantic event identity, semantic event digest, and graph commit cursor that identifies one semantic event epoch across stream boundaries.
definition.formal_voice: ExactSemanticEventReference = (semantic_event_id, semantic_event_digest, semantic_cursor), and every component must match one stored semantic event.
definition.operational_interpretation: Reject a governance join when any tuple component is absent, stale, ambiguous, or belongs to a different event.
definition.plain_language_voice: The three-part exact address of one version of semantic state.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy Lab uses this reference so a governance event cannot attach to a convenient but different node version.
definition.boundary: Subject ID, cursor, event ID, or digest alone is not an exact reference.

records.challenge_or_refresh_route: CyberAlchemy Lab semantic and governance stream owners

definition.normative_voice: This pack reuses CAV2-D23 without amendment: kind, status, evidence confidence, commitment, provenance, owner, and residue remain separate authority-lifecycle dimensions.
definition.formal_voice: L(a) = (kind, status, evidence, commitment, provenance, owner, residue), with no implicit cross-axis movement.
definition.operational_interpretation: Record which governance dimension changed and leave every other dimension unchanged unless an explicit typed coupling says otherwise.
definition.plain_language_voice: Useful, trusted, finished, owned, and canonical are different claims.
definition.domain_context_voice: The governed-node view carries separate fields so node maturity cannot impersonate evidence or authority.
definition.boundary: The axis is not a complete status taxonomy and does not turn every artifact into an ontology node.

definition.normative_voice: EvidenceConfidence is the CAV2-D23 evidence axis applied to how strongly current evidence supports the semantic claim represented by one exact ontology subject epoch.
definition.formal_voice: evidence_confidence(subject_epoch) is independent of commitment_confidence, lifecycle, status, authority, and challenge outcome.
definition.operational_interpretation: Update the evidence axis through governance events bound to the exact semantic event; do not rewrite semantic state.
definition.plain_language_voice: How confident the evidence lets us be about this exact version of meaning.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy Lab stores evidence confidence in the governance stream, even though it assesses a semantic claim.
definition.boundary: Do not call this semantic confidence, because that phrase hides its evidence basis and suggests confidence lives in semantic state.

definition.normative_voice: CommitmentConfidence is the CAV2-D23 commitment axis applied to the responsible owner's declared willingness to rely on or act from one exact ontology subject epoch.
definition.formal_voice: commitment_confidence(subject_epoch) is independent of evidence_confidence, lifecycle, status, promotion, and authority effect.
definition.operational_interpretation: Record owner commitment as a governance posture and never infer it from evidence strength or maturity.
definition.plain_language_voice: How strongly the owner is prepared to rely on this exact version.
definition.domain_context_voice: A CyberAlchemy owner may have high commitment to a low-evidence premise, but the two axes remain visible.
definition.boundary: Do not call this governance confidence, because governance state contains many non-confidence fields and does not form one aggregate score.

definition.normative_voice: EvidenceStrength is an evidence-object assessment of how directly, reliably, and currently one evidence item supports or contradicts one stated claim under declared observation conditions.
definition.formal_voice: evidence_strength(evidence, claim, conditions) is an assessment input to evidence_confidence; it is not evidence_confidence itself.
definition.operational_interpretation: Assess evidence items first, preserve provenance and conditions, then let an owner-controlled assessment update evidence confidence separately.
definition.plain_language_voice: How much support one piece of evidence actually provides for one claim.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy Lab can compare evidence items without collapsing their strength into the node's confidence or the owner's commitment.
definition.boundary: Evidence strength is not truth, confidence, commitment, authority, maturity, or a promotion verdict.

definition.normative_voice: TypedResidue is CAV2-D18 residue attached to an ontology subject or operation with its source operation, expected preservation condition, observed remainder, residue type, evidence, owner route, and treatment stated explicitly.
definition.formal_voice: TypedResidue = (source_operation, expected_condition, observed_remainder, residue_type, evidence_ref, owner_route, treatment).
definition.operational_interpretation: Preserve any unknown, conflicting, unmapped, or unvalidated structure as typed residue and route it instead of dropping it into an untyped property bag.
definition.plain_language_voice: The meaningful leftover, recorded with what it is and who must handle it.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy Lab uses typed residue for schema gaps, stale joins, migration mismatches, unresolved challenges, and authority gaps.
definition.boundary: Residue is not any uncertainty, automatic failure, novelty proof, generic notes, or permission to proceed.

definition.normative_voice: OntologyLifecycleState is the semantic state of whether an OntologySubject exists for use at a selected cursor under one owner-defined closed vocabulary.
definition.formal_voice: lifecycle(subject,cursor) belongs to one closed vocabulary and is independent of candidate status, maturity, promotion, projection state, and authority posture.
definition.operational_interpretation: Calculate lifecycle from the subject's semantic event stream and use it when determining node membership and relation endpoint integrity.
definition.plain_language_voice: Whether this node or relation exists for use at this point in its history.
definition.domain_context_voice: The exact lifecycle values remain an open owner decision before executable schema authoring.
definition.boundary: Lifecycle does not mean reviewed, trusted, promoted, projected, mature, or authoritative.

definition.normative_voice: A UseObligation is a typed condition that a consumer must preserve or satisfy when using one ontology subject for a stated purpose.
definition.formal_voice: use(subject,purpose) is permitted only if every applicable obligation(subject,purpose) is satisfied or explicitly blocked.
definition.operational_interpretation: Carry obligations in semantic state and evaluate them in the consuming context without converting them into authority.
definition.plain_language_voice: A rule the consumer must follow when it uses this meaning.
definition.domain_context_voice: A context projection retains the obligations needed for its intended use even when it filters other fields.
definition.boundary: A use obligation is not a governance verdict, global policy, implied permission, or hidden implementation requirement.

definition.normative_voice: A ForbiddenCollapse is an explicit declaration that one term, field, state, relation, or authority posture must not be treated as equivalent to another named concept.
definition.formal_voice: ForbiddenCollapse(a,b) asserts a is not equivalent to b for the declared context and intended use.
definition.operational_interpretation: Use the declarations to design negative fixtures that reject field aliases, inferred relationships, or state transitions that erase required distinctions.
definition.plain_language_voice: A warning that two similar-looking things must stay different.
definition.domain_context_voice: The governed-node model uses these rules to keep confidence axes, lifecycle, maturity, authority, challenge, residue, and projections separate.
definition.boundary: It is not a claim that the concepts never interact; explicit typed couplings may relate them without merging them.

definition.normative_voice: This pack reuses CAV2-D35 without amendment: provenance is the declared typed origin and transformation chain for the ontology subject, event, projection, evidence, decision, or residue.
definition.formal_voice: Prov(x) = [(source_i, relation_i, operation_i, owner_i, posture_i)]*; missing segments are typed residue.
definition.operational_interpretation: Retain source references, transformations, owners, and posture changes so every calculated view can be audited to its origin.
definition.plain_language_voice: The receipt trail for where the object came from and how it changed.
definition.domain_context_voice: Governance events carry typed provenance without turning a complete source trail into proof or authority.
definition.boundary: Provenance is not proof, trust, validation, authority, or credit assignment by itself.

definition.normative_voice: A GovernanceEvent is an immutable typed record of one governance-state change or observation in a governance-owned stream, bound to one semantic event epoch through an ExactSemanticEventReference.
definition.formal_voice: GovernanceEvent = (event_identity, governance_stream_identity, exact_semantic_reference, complete_resulting_governance_state, ordering_metadata).
definition.operational_interpretation: Validate the exact semantic reference and stream continuity before using the event to calculate governance state.
definition.plain_language_voice: A permanent governance update about one exact version of a node or relation.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy Lab keeps this event outside the semantic subject stream so governance owners cannot silently edit meaning.
definition.boundary: A governance event is not a semantic event, authority grant, promotion verdict, or replay source for semantic state.
